question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
Morbid compulsion to consume alcohol continuously
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Dipsomania.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Dipsomania" means an uncontrollable, morbid craving or compulsion to consume alcohol continuously. (शराब पीने की असाधारण लत/इच्छा)
◦ Example: His dipsomania eventually cost him his job and his family.

• The word is formed from the Greek roots "dipsa" (thirst) and "mania" (madness/obsession), literally "thirst-madness".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Satyromania (पुरुषों में अत्यधिक कामेच्छा): An excessive, uncontrollable sexual desire in men.

• Option 2: Maniac (उन्मत्त व्यक्ति): A person who is violently insane or wildly enthusiastic about something; it is a general term, not specific to alcohol.

• Option 3: Kleptomania (चोरी करने की असाधारण लत): An irresistible urge to steal, typically without economic motive.

NOTE

• Related "-mania" words often asked in SSC: Pyromania (compulsion to set fires), Megalomania (obsession with one's own power), Monomania (obsession with one thing), Bibliomania (excessive love of books).

• Do not confuse Dipsomania (compulsion to drink) with Teetotalism (complete abstinence from alcohol), its near-opposite.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.
The painting was admired by art enthusiasts from around the world.
option_1: The painting was being admired by art enthusiasts from around the world.
option_2: Art enthusiasts from around the world admired the painting.
option_3: Art enthusiasts from around the world have admired the painting.
option_4: The painting has been admired by art enthusiasts from around the world.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Art enthusiasts from around the world admired the painting.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence "The painting was admired by art enthusiasts from around the world" is in the Passive Voice, Simple Past Tense (was/were + V3).

• Rule — Simple Past Tense:
◦ Passive: Object + was/were + V3 + by + Subject
◦ Active: Subject + V2 + Object

• Applying the rule: the agent "art enthusiasts from around the world" becomes the subject; the past participle "admired" is converted to the simple past form "admired" (same form, since "admire" is a regular verb); and "the painting" becomes the object.
◦ Active: Art enthusiasts from around the world admired the painting.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "was being admired" is the passive form of the Past Continuous Tense, not the Simple Past Tense of the given sentence.

• Option 3 is incorrect because "have admired" is the active form of the Present Perfect Tense, which changes the time frame of the original sentence.

• Option 4 is incorrect because "has been admired" is still in the Passive Voice (Present Perfect), not the active voice, and the question demands an active-voice conversion.

NOTE

• While converting passive to active voice, the tense of the sentence must never change — only the arrangement of subject, object and verb form changes.

• Common tense-passive forms: Simple Present – is/am/are + V3; Simple Past – was/were + V3; Simple Future – will/shall + be + V3.

question:
Select the word segment that can substitute the bracketed word segment correctly and complete the sentence meaningfully.
(Each participant have) performed well.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Each participant has.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject "Each participant" is a singular indefinite pronoun-noun combination; words like "each", "every", "either", "neither" are always followed by a singular verb, even if they refer to more than one person collectively.

• Rule — Subject-Verb Agreement with "Each/Every":
◦ Each/Every + singular noun + singular verb (has/is/was)

• Since the sentence is describing a completed action with present relevance (Present Perfect Tense: has/have + V3), and the subject is singular, the correct auxiliary is "has".
◦ Corrected sentence: Each participant has performed well.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Each participant was" is incorrect because "was" would require a following V3 in passive sense or an adjective/noun complement, not "performed" as a main verb in active perfect sense; it does not fit the Present Perfect structure needed here.

• Option 3: "Each participant have been" is incorrect because "have" is a plural auxiliary, which does not agree with the singular subject "each participant".

• Option 4: "Each participant were" is incorrect for the same reason — "were" is a plural/subjunctive verb form and cannot agree with the singular "each participant".

NOTE

• Other determiners that always take a singular verb: each, every, either, neither, everyone, everybody, everything, someone, anyone, no one.

• Example: "Every boy and girl has submitted the assignment" (not "have").

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.
Fatima was at her wits' end trying to decide on a serene place for spending the holidays in.
option_1: So worried, confused or annoyed that she does not know what to do next
option_2: So worried, confused or annoyed that she became unconscious
option_3: So calm and composed that she knows what to do next
option_4: So worried, confused or annoyed that she insulted others for no reason
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. So worried, confused or annoyed that she does not know what to do next.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "at one's wits' end" means to be so worried, confused or perplexed by a problem that one does not know what to do next. (इतना परेशान या असमंजस में होना कि कुछ समझ न आए)
◦ Example: After searching everywhere for her lost passport, she was at her wits' end.

• The word "wits" refers to one's mental faculties/reasoning ability; being at their "end" means those faculties have been exhausted in trying to solve a problem.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 is incorrect because the idiom has nothing to do with losing consciousness; it describes mental confusion, not a physical fainting spell.

• Option 3 is incorrect because it gives the opposite meaning — the idiom denotes a state of worry and confusion, not calm and composure.

• Option 4 is incorrect because the idiom does not imply insulting others; it is purely about the person's own confused mental state.

NOTE

• Other idioms of confusion/worry frequently asked in SSC: "To be at sea" (to be confused), "To be in a fix" (to be in a difficult situation), "To rack one's brains" (to think very hard about something).

• Do not confuse "at one's wits' end" with "to have one's wits about oneself", which means to be alert and think clearly, i.e., the opposite meaning.

question:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.
P. having the opportunity of observing people's
Q. we respect and appreciate their point of views
R. the advantage of travelling different places and
S. culture, custom and lifestyle, is that
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. RPSQ.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correctly arranged sentence reads: "The advantage of travelling different places and having the opportunity of observing people's culture, custom and lifestyle, is that we respect and appreciate their point of views."

• Rule for para/sentence jumbles: identify the part that can logically begin the sentence (usually the subject of the main clause), then trace the natural chain of ideas — a noun phrase introduced in one part is usually completed or explained in the part that follows it.
◦ R introduces the subject: "the advantage of travelling different places and..."
◦ P continues the subject with a parallel gerund phrase: "...having the opportunity of observing people's..."
◦ S completes the list of things observed ("culture, custom and lifestyle") and supplies the linking verb "is that"
◦ Q supplies the result clause that "is that" demands: "we respect and appreciate their point of views."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: RQPS is incorrect because it places Q (the result clause beginning "we respect...") directly after R, before the phrase "having the opportunity of observing people's culture..." has even been introduced, making the sentence incoherent.

• Option 2: PSQR is incorrect because it begins with P, which starts with the gerund "having", a construction that cannot logically open the sentence without the subject established by R first.

• Option 4: SQPR is incorrect because it begins with S ("culture, custom and lifestyle, is that"), which makes no sense as an opening line since "culture, custom and lifestyle" has no antecedent yet.

NOTE

• In parts/jumbled-sentence questions, always look for a grammatical subject that can stand independently at the start, and match pronouns/possessives (their, its) to the nouns they refer to, to fix the correct sequence.

• Parallel structures (here, two gerund phrases "travelling..." and "having...") joined by "and" are a strong clue that they belong together as consecutive parts.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Mischievious.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Mischievous", not "Mischievious". It means playfully troublesome or fond of causing minor trouble.
◦ Example: The mischievous child hid his sister's shoes as a prank.

• Spelling key: MISCHIEV + OUS — the word ends directly in "-ievous"; there is no extra "i" before "-ous", even though the word is often mispronounced with an extra syllable.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Accommodate" is correctly spelt — note the double "c" and double "m".

• Option 3: "Millennium" is correctly spelt — note the double "l" and double "n".

• Option 4: "Privilege" is correctly spelt — note it is "-lege", not "-ledge".

NOTE

• Other words commonly mis-spelt with a wrongly inserted extra syllable, similar to "mischievous": "Grievous" (not "grievious"); "Devious" is correctly spelt with the "i" since it comes from "deviate".

• Frequently confused double-letter spellings in SSC exams: Accommodate, Millennium, Embarrass, Occurrence, Committee.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Taut
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Tight.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Taut" means stretched or pulled tight; not slack. (कसा हुआ/तना हुआ)
◦ Example: The gymnast kept the rope taut before beginning her routine.

• Its closest synonym among the given options is "Tight", which also means stretched firmly with no slack.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Slack (ढीला): Means loose or not tightly stretched — this is actually the antonym of "taut".

• Option 3: Torn (फटा हुआ): Means ripped or pulled apart, unrelated to tightness.

• Option 4: Flaccid (ढीला/शिथिल): Means soft, limp and lacking firmness — again closer to the opposite of "taut".

NOTE

• "Taut" is commonly used in both literal contexts (a taut rope/wire) and figurative contexts (a taut plot/script, meaning tightly constructed with no loose ends).

• Related word pairs often confused in SSC vocabulary questions: Taut vs Taunt (taunt = to mock/tease), which are spelt similarly but have entirely different meanings.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.
He will be made President by the people.
option_1: People will be making him the President.
option_2: The people will make him President.
option_3: By the people, he shall be made the President.
option_4: He will be made President by the people.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. The people will make him President.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence "He will be made President by the people" is in the Passive Voice, Simple Future Tense (will/shall + be + V3).

• Rule — Simple Future Tense:
◦ Passive: Object + will/shall + be + V3 + by + Subject
◦ Active: Subject + will/shall + V1 + Object

• Applying the rule: the agent "the people" becomes the subject; "be made" is converted to the base form "make"; and "he" becomes the object "him", with the complement "President" retained.
◦ Active: The people will make him President.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "will be making" is the active form of the Future Continuous Tense, which changes the tense of the original sentence.

• Option 3 is incorrect because it retains the passive structure "shall be made" and merely reorders the sentence — it is not converted to active voice at all.

• Option 4 is simply the original passive sentence unchanged, so it cannot be the active-voice version.

NOTE

• While converting Simple Future passive to active, the modal (will/shall) is retained but moved before the subject-verb, and "be + V3" reduces to the plain base verb (V1).

• Common error: students often forget to change the object pronoun form correctly — "he" (subject case) becomes "him" (object case) in the active sentence.

question: Which of the following idioms means 'to steal from a shop'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Five-finger discount.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Five-finger discount" is an informal/slang expression meaning to steal something, especially from a shop, as if the five fingers of the hand were used to take the item "free of cost". (दुकान से चोरी करना)
◦ Example: He got himself a new phone case with a five-finger discount from the mall.

• The phrase humorously implies that using one's fingers (i.e., stealing) results in getting something at no price, a mock "discount".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Golden opportunity (सुनहरा अवसर): Means an excellent chance that should not be missed.

• Option 2: Green thumb (बागवानी में कुशल): Means a natural talent for gardening/growing plants.

• Option 4: Black sheep (कुल कलंक): Means a disreputable or disgraceful member of a family or group.

NOTE

• Other body-part idioms frequently tested in SSC: "Cold shoulder" (unfriendly treatment), "Keep an ear to the ground" (stay alert to news), "Foot the bill" (pay for something).

• Do not confuse "Five-finger discount" (steal) with genuine commercial terms like "bulk discount" or "cash discount", which refer to legitimate price reductions.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
I are dancing with my husband at my sister's wedding.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. I are dancing.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The error lies in the segment "I are dancing". The subject "I" always takes the auxiliary verb "am", never "are" or "is".

• Rule — Subject-Verb Agreement with Pronoun "I":
◦ I + am (+ V-ing / adjective / noun)
◦ You/We/They + are
◦ He/She/It + is

• The sentence should correctly read: "I am dancing with my husband at my sister's wedding."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "husband at my" is grammatically correct as part of the prepositional phrase and contains no error.

• Option 2: "sister's wedding" correctly uses the possessive apostrophe with a singular noun and contains no error.

• Option 3: "with my" is a correct preposition-possessive combination and contains no error.

NOTE

• "Am" is used exclusively with the first-person singular pronoun "I" in the present tense — this is a very frequently tested SSC error-spotting trap.

• Similarly watch for: "He are" (should be "He is"); "They is" (should be "They are"); "We is" (should be "We are").

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
The tea at this café is best than at the Costa Café in our office.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. is best than.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The error lies in the segment "is best than". When only two things are compared, the comparative degree of the adjective must be used, not the superlative degree.

• Rule — Degrees of Comparison:
◦ Comparative (for 2 things): Adjective + er/more + than
◦ Superlative (for 3 or more things): the + Adjective + est/most

• Since only two items are being compared — "the tea at this café" and "at the Costa Café" — the correct comparative form is "better than", not "best than". The sentence should read: "The tea at this café is better than at the Costa Café in our office."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "at the Costa Café" is grammatically correct as the second element of comparison and contains no error.

• Option 2: "The tea at this café" correctly forms the subject of the sentence and contains no error.

• Option 4: "in our office" is a correct prepositional phrase modifying "Costa Café" and contains no error.

NOTE

• "Best" (superlative of "good") is used only when comparing three or more items, e.g., "This is the best tea among all the cafés in the city."

• The word "than" is always paired with a comparative form ("better than", "taller than"), never with a superlative form.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Miserable
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Cheerful.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Miserable" means extremely unhappy, uncomfortable or wretched in condition. (दुखी/कष्टमय)
◦ Example: He felt miserable after failing the examination.

• Its direct opposite among the given options is "Cheerful", which means noticeably happy and optimistic.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Melodious (सुरीला): Means pleasant-sounding, relating to music — unrelated to happiness/unhappiness.

• Option 2: Settled (स्थिर/व्यवस्थित): Means established or resolved — not an opposite of "miserable" in the emotional sense.

• Option 3: Restrained (संयमित): Means kept under control or held back — describes behaviour, not an emotional opposite of misery.

NOTE

• Synonyms of "miserable" often tested alongside: wretched, forlorn, despondent, dejected.

• Other antonym pairs frequently asked: Miserable × Jubilant/Elated/Content, all meaning happy or satisfied.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Confiscate
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Seize.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Confiscate" means to take or seize someone's property with authority, often as a penalty. (जब्त करना)
◦ Example: The customs officials confiscated the smuggled goods at the airport.

• Its closest synonym among the given options is "Seize", which also means to take possession of something forcibly, especially by legal right or authority.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Restock (फिर से भंडार भरना): Means to replenish supplies — the opposite action of taking something away.

• Option 2: Destroy (नष्ट करना): Means to ruin or demolish completely — confiscating something does not necessarily destroy it.

• Option 4: Titivate (सजाना-सँवारना): Means to make oneself or something look attractive with minor enhancements — completely unrelated in meaning.

NOTE

• Related words: Impound (to seize and hold, often used for vehicles), Requisition (to officially demand the use of), Sequester (to legally take possession of property until a debt is paid).

• Do not confuse "Confiscate" with "Donate" or "Distribute", which mean the opposite — giving away rather than taking.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given word.
Edible
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. nutritive.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Edible" means fit or safe to be eaten; suitable for consumption as food. (खाने योग्य)
◦ Example: Mushrooms must be identified carefully, as not every wild variety is edible.

• Among the given options, "nutritive" (relating to nourishment/providing nourishment as food) is the word most closely associated with something being fit to eat, making it the best available choice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Noisome (दुर्गंधयुक्त/हानिकारक): Means having an extremely unpleasant smell, or harmful — the opposite connotation of something fit to eat.

• Option 2: Mortal (नश्वर/घातक): Means subject to death, or (as an adjective) causing death — unrelated to edibility, and if anything suggests danger.

• Option 3: Noxious (हानिकारक/विषैला): Means harmful, poisonous or unpleasant — again the opposite sense of something safe to consume.

NOTE

• Do not confuse "Edible" (fit to eat) with "Eligible" (qualified/entitled) — a common SSC distractor pair due to similar spelling.

• Words with the opposite meaning of "edible": Inedible, Poisonous, Toxic, Noxious — useful to recall for antonym-based questions on this word.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
There are many factories in the operative area of the city.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. industrial.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the context of the sentence, "operative area" (an area where factories are functioning/in operation) is best substituted by "industrial", meaning relating to or characterised by industries/factories. (औद्योगिक)
◦ Example: The new manufacturing units have been set up in the industrial area on the outskirts of the city.

• The sentence is describing a zone identified by the presence of factories, and "industrial area" is the standard, natural collocation used for such a zone in English.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: Serviceable (उपयोगी/काम चलाऊ): Means usable or in working condition — describes a state of an object, not a type of area.

• Option 3: Industrious (परिश्रमी): Means hard-working or diligent — describes a person's character, not an area with factories; a common trap due to its similarity to "industrial".

• Option 4: Mechanical (यांत्रिक): Means relating to machines or operated by machinery — describes a process or device, not a geographical area.

NOTE

• Do not confuse "Industrial" (relating to industries, e.g., industrial area) with "Industrious" (hard-working, e.g., an industrious student) — this pair is one of the most common confusable-word traps in SSC exams.

• Other similarly confused pairs: Economic vs Economical, Historic vs Historical, Sensible vs Sensitive.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the bracketed word in the following sentence to fill in the blank.
The elaborate syllabi had to be ________(summarised) to make a presentation in the UGC assessment meeting.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. recapitulated.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Recapitulate" means to summarise or state again briefly the main points of something, which is the closest synonym of the bracketed word "summarised". (संक्षेप में दोहराना)
◦ Example: The professor recapitulated the elaborate syllabi into a short presentation for the UGC assessment meeting.

• The sentence requires a word meaning "made brief/condensed", since the elaborate (detailed, lengthy) syllabi had to be shortened for the presentation.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Expanded (विस्तृत करना): Means to make something larger or more detailed — the opposite of summarising.

• Option 3: Prolonged (लंबा करना): Means to extend the duration of something — again the opposite sense of shortening.

• Option 4: Lengthened (लंबा करना): Means to make something longer — also opposite to the required meaning of condensing.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "summarise" useful for SSC vocabulary: Abridge, Condense, Encapsulate, Epitomise, Précis.

• Do not confuse "Recapitulate" (to summarise) with "Recapture" (to capture again) or "Reciprocate" (to respond in kind) — all share the "re-" prefix but differ completely in meaning.

question:
Identify the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the following sentence and select its correct spelling from the given options.
I receieved a parcel in the mail today.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. received.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "receieved" in the given sentence is misspelt; the correct spelling is "received".

• Spelling key: the word follows the rule "i before e except after c" — since the letter before "ei/ie" here is "c", the spelling must be "ceive" (e before i), giving re-c-e-i-v-e-d, not "re-c-i-e-v-e-d".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "recived" is incorrect — it wrongly omits the letter "e" after "c" altogether.

• Option 3: "recieved" is incorrect — this repeats the same "i before e after c" error as the original misspelt word in the sentence.

• Option 4: "receaved" is incorrect — it wrongly substitutes "ea" in place of the correct "ei".

NOTE

• The rule "i before e, except after c" applies to words like: believe, achieve, relieve (i before e) vs receive, deceive, ceiling, perceive (e before i, after c).

• Common exceptions to remember separately: weird, seize, either, neither, science, species.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words.
The question papers are placed in the lockers of the school in a way that they can't be reached.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. are inaccessible.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Inaccessible" means unable to be reached or entered; not accessible, which is the exact one-word substitute for the underlined phrase "can't be reached". (न पहुँचा जा सकने योग्य)
◦ Example: The old manuscript is kept in a vault and is inaccessible to the public.

• The sentence describes question papers locked away such that they cannot be reached/obtained, which is precisely what "inaccessible" conveys.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Irrepressible (अनियंत्रित/न दबाया जा सकने वाला): Means unable to be controlled or restrained (usually describing enthusiasm or emotion), unrelated to physical reachability.

• Option 3: Affordable (वहनीय): Means inexpensive enough to be within one's financial means — a completely different meaning relating to cost, not access.

• Option 4: Affable (मिलनसार): Means friendly and easy to talk to, describing a person's temperament — unrelated to the context of reaching an object.

NOTE

• Do not confuse "Inaccessible" (cannot be reached) with "Inaccurate" (not correct/precise) — a common look-alike trap.

• Related one-word substitutes: "Accessible" (that which can be reached/entered), "Impregnable" (that which cannot be captured by force).

question:
Select the most appropriate homophone to fill in the blank.
He has the ________ to express his thoughts.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. right.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence requires a word meaning an entitlement or a just claim to do something, which is expressed by "right" — as in "the right to express his thoughts", i.e., the freedom or entitlement to voice one's opinion.

• Rule: "Right", "write" and "rite" are homophones (words that sound alike but differ in spelling and meaning): right = entitlement/correct; write = to put words on paper; rite = a religious/ceremonial practice.

• Applying this rule to the sentence: only "right" fits grammatically (as a noun following "the") and semantically (an entitlement to express thoughts).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "ride" means to travel on/in a vehicle or animal — it is not even a homophone of the others and does not fit the sentence's meaning.

• Option 3: "write" means to inscribe words; "the write to express" is grammatically meaningless, since "write" is a verb and cannot follow "the" as a noun here.

• Option 4: "rite" means a formal religious or traditional ceremony/custom, e.g. "funeral rite" — it does not fit the meaning of "entitlement" required in the sentence.

NOTE

• Other commonly tested homophone sets in SSC: there/their/they're, its/it's, whose/who's, peace/piece, principal/principle.

• Remember: "right" used as a noun commonly appears in phrases like "human rights", "the right to vote", "the right to education".

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
An order of law requiring people to remain indoors
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Curfew.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Curfew" means an official order or regulation requiring people to remain indoors, typically during specified hours (often at night or during an emergency). (कर्फ्यू / निषेधाज्ञा)
◦ Example: The authorities imposed a curfew in the city following the riots.

• This is a legal/administrative order specifically tied to staying indoors, distinguishing it from more general terms.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Restriction (प्रतिबंध): Means a general limitation placed on an action or activity — too broad and not specific to staying indoors.

• Option 3: Limit (सीमा): Means a boundary or maximum extent of something — a general term unrelated specifically to an order to stay indoors.

• Option 4: Check in: Means to register one's arrival at a hotel, airport, etc. — completely unrelated to a legal order to remain indoors.

NOTE

• Related legal/administrative one-word substitutes often tested in SSC: "Martial law" (military rule imposed during an emergency), "Moratorium" (a temporary prohibition of an activity), "Embargo" (an official ban on trade).

• "Curfew" is often confused with "lockdown", which is a broader restriction on movement, not necessarily confined to specific hours.

In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Tea prices in the domestic (1)__________ continue to rule high in the current year despite the expectation of a higher production as compared to the previous year. During the past three months, tea prices have been (2)__________ with the prices of other companies. Unlike last year, tea prices have generally shown (3) __________, when tea prices rose dramatically, this year, prices seem to have (4) __________ at a rather high level. In the subsequent four months, the (5)__________ average price showed a downtrend.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. market.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage discusses tea prices, production, and comparison "with the prices of other companies" — this is clearly a discussion of commercial/trade activity, for which the standard collocation is "domestic market", meaning the market within one's own country as opposed to international/export markets.

• Rule for cloze passages: always read the sentences before and after the blank to identify the exact context/collocation required, rather than picking a word that merely fits grammatically.

• "Tea prices in the domestic market continue to rule high" is a standard economic-news phrase referring to prices within the country's trading system.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "area" is too vague/geographic and does not form the standard collocation "domestic area" in an economic/pricing context.

• Option 3: "zone" similarly refers to a geographic or administrative division, not a trading/pricing system, and does not fit the context of prices.

• Option 4: "field" refers to a subject/discipline or a literal piece of land, neither of which fits the discussion of tea prices and trade.

NOTE

• Common collocations with "domestic" in economic passages: domestic market, domestic production, domestic demand, domestic consumption, domestic trade.

• The opposite of "domestic market" is the "international/export market", a contrast frequently used in such comprehension passages.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. aligning.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence states that during the past three months, tea prices have been (2)__________ with the prices of other companies, i.e., moving in line/step with them. "Aligning" means coming into or being in correct or agreed relative position with something else, which precisely fits the sense of prices matching/tracking each other.

• Rule for cloze passages: the preposition following the blank — here "with" — is a strong clue; "align with" is a fixed, natural collocation meaning to correspond or match.

• "Tea prices have been aligning with the prices of other companies" means the two sets of prices have been moving similarly/in tandem.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "favouring" does not collocate naturally with "with" in this sense and would imply bias, which does not fit a discussion of price levels tracking each other.

• Option 3: "countering" means opposing or acting against, which contradicts the idea of prices matching/tracking together.

• Option 4: "encountering" means to unexpectedly meet or face something (usually a problem), which does not fit the context of prices moving together.

NOTE

• "Align with" is a common collocation in business/economic English meaning to match or correspond to a standard or another set of figures.

• Contrast with "counter", which typically collocates with "oppose", "resist" or "challenge" — the opposite sense of matching.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Tea prices in the domestic (1)__________ continue to rule high in the current year despite the expectation of a higher production as compared to the previous year. During the past three months, tea prices have been (2)__________ with the prices of other companies. Unlike last year, tea prices have generally shown (3) __________, when tea prices rose dramatically, this year, prices seem to have (4) __________ at a rather high level. In the subsequent four months, the (5)__________ average price showed a downtrend.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. an uptrend.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: "Unlike last year, tea prices have generally shown (3)__________, when tea prices rose dramatically..." The clause after the comma explicitly explains what happened last year — prices "rose dramatically" — so the blank must be a noun meaning a rising trend, i.e., "an uptrend".

• Rule for cloze passages: when a blank is immediately followed by a clause beginning with "when" that restates or explains the blank, that clause is a direct definitional clue to the missing word.

• "Tea prices have generally shown an uptrend, when [i.e., a period in which] tea prices rose dramatically" logically connects the blank to the stated rise in prices.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "an inflow" refers to an incoming flow (commonly of funds/goods), which does not describe a price trend.

• Option 2: "an innate" is grammatically incorrect here, as "innate" is an adjective (meaning inborn/natural) and cannot be used as a noun after the article "an" in this slot.

• Option 3: "a reduction" means a decrease, which directly contradicts the following clause stating that "tea prices rose dramatically".

NOTE

• "Uptrend" and "downtrend" are standard business/economic terms describing sustained upward or downward movement in prices or markets, and both terms appear in the same passage ("the average price showed a downtrend"), confirming this is the register/vocabulary of the passage.

• Do not confuse "innate" (adjective: inborn) with nouns like "increase" or "rise" — a frequent grammatical trap in SSC cloze questions.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Tea prices in the domestic (1)__________ continue to rule high in the current year despite the expectation of a higher production as compared to the previous year. During the past three months, tea prices have been (2)__________ with the prices of other companies. Unlike last year, tea prices have generally shown (3) __________, when tea prices rose dramatically, this year, prices seem to have (4) __________ at a rather high level. In the subsequent four months, the (5)__________ average price showed a downtrend.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. stabilised.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: "...this year, prices seem to have (4)__________ at a rather high level." The phrase "at a rather high level" indicates that prices have settled/steadied at that high point, rather than continuing to change — this sense is best captured by "stabilised", meaning to become steady/settled and stop fluctuating.

• Rule for cloze passages: the preposition "at" following the blank is a strong clue — "stabilise at [a level/value]" is a standard, fixed collocation used in describing prices, exchange rates, and economic indicators.

• "Prices seem to have stabilised at a rather high level" means prices stopped rising/falling and remained steady, though at a high point.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "moderated" means to become or make less extreme, which would suggest prices came down somewhat — this does not naturally collocate with "at a level" in the same fixed sense as "stabilised".

• Option 3: "equated" means to consider one thing as equal to or the same as another, which does not fit the sense of a price settling at a level.

• Option 4: "abated" means to become less intense/reduce, again implying a fall, which contradicts the description of prices remaining at "a rather high level".

NOTE

• "Stabilise at" is a very common phrase in economic and business English, e.g., "inflation stabilised at 5%", "the exchange rate stabilised at a lower value".

• Do not confuse "stabilise" (to become steady) with words implying a fall, such as "abate" or "moderate", which are frequent distractors in this kind of question.

In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Tea prices in the domestic (1)__________ continue to rule high in the current year despite the expectation of a higher production as compared to the previous year. During the past three months, tea prices have been (2)__________ with the prices of other companies. Unlike last year, tea prices have generally shown (3) __________, when tea prices rose dramatically, this year, prices seem to have (4) __________ at a rather high level. In the subsequent four months, the (5)__________ average price showed a downtrend.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. monthly.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage earlier refers to "the past three months" and "the subsequent four months", showing that the discussion is tracking price movements on a month-by-month basis. The final sentence — "In the subsequent four months, the (5)__________ average price showed a downtrend" — logically continues this pattern, requiring "monthly" to describe the average calculated each month.

• Rule for cloze passages: maintain consistency with the time-frame/register already established earlier in the same passage; since the passage has been discussing figures in terms of "months" throughout, the missing adjective must also relate to "month".

• "The monthly average price showed a downtrend" means the average price, computed every month over those four months, was trending downward.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "half yearly" refers to a six-month period, which does not match the "four months" time-frame stated in the same sentence.

• Option 3: "weekly" refers to a seven-day period, which is inconsistent with the passage's consistent use of "months" as its unit of time throughout.

• Option 4: "yearly" refers to a twelve-month period, which is too long a span to be meaningfully computed "in the subsequent four months".

NOTE

• Time-frequency adjectives frequently tested in SSC cloze passages: daily, weekly, fortnightly, monthly, quarterly, half-yearly, annually/yearly.

• Always cross-check such words against explicit numeric time references already given in the passage (here, "three months" and "four months"), as the SSC key is almost always internally consistent with such details.
